text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Energy Regulatory Commission is expected to discuss a 10 percent rise in electricity prices from next month in line with May monthly inflation of 5.6 percent and an upcoming currency board peg at 1,000 levs per mark from July 1. @
-- Bulgaria's Gross Domestic Product fell a real 11.7 percent in the first quarter of this year to 2.182 trillion levs at current prices, National Statistics Institute figures showed.
-- Bulgaria will seek to double its quotas for wine exports to European Union member countries next year, Trade minister Valentin Vassilev said.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would cut its main interest rate to an effective annual 10.60 percent from 16.30 percent, from Monday. @
-- Bulgaria expects some $570 million proceeds from tourist operations this year, deputy Trade Minister Roumen Draganov said.

-- Bulgaria will open all secret police files of the communist era under a draft law which the cabinet plans to be submit to parliament in the next two months, deputy prime minister Vesselin Metodiev said.
-- Bulgarian customs officers at the Bulgarian-Macedonian border checkpoint of Gyuishevo said they had seized four kilogrammes of heroin hidden in an Albanian-registered Mercedes car.
-- Bulgaria is expected to seek a new debt rating in September in line with preparations to issue Eurobonds, a Finance ministry official said.
-- The average monthly wage in Bulgaria's state sector stood at 142,534 levs in May, the National Statistics Institute said. @
-- Bulgaria's Industry ministry said it had sealed privatisation deals worth seven billion levs in the last three months.
-- Bulgaria's northeast Black Sea holiday resort of Zlatni Pyasatsi said it would seek some 2.25 billion lev loan to fund its restructuring programme. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
